strengths: The paper is well-written and well-structured.
The paper presents a clear method similar to diffusion methods in other domains. The technical details are discussed in detail. It seems straightforward to reproduce the results.
The presented problem is essential and timely. In particular, synthetic time series generation is critical for foundation model development, as the authors mention in the discussion.

The works did comprehensive evaluation on unconditional and conditional generation tasks, taking both lower-order and higher-order statistics into account. The proposed approach shows superior performance over existing approaches on both tasks across the datasets considered in the work. In addition the work also did comprehensive over different hyper-parameters variations and ablations to reveal the impact of different components to the model.
The presentation quality of the work is good and the proposed method of the work is easy to follow.
The paper is easy to read and the experiments are comprehensive.
weaknesses: It is worth discussing more the key differences to other diffusion-based models such as Diffusion-ts and TimeDiff. Additionally, it is worth expanding metrics, such as consistency and diversity, as discussed in the TSGM framework.
Limitations and fairness are not discussed enough. In particular, can generated data be biased with respect to conditional metadata?
It would be great to have more details on the design choices of the decoder and $\epsilon_\theta$. Do other architectures significantly affect the performance of the method?
DDPM or VAE for time series generation is not new. Most techniques used are also from prior works.

It’s well-known that VAE is considered 1-step DDPM. The motivation and reasoning in line 144-154 is very unconvincing. It’s still unclear why DDPM is good at handling time series data, why VAE, as a special case is DDPM, can bring more to the table. Also, citing unpublished and prior venue’s rejections as SOTA method is not convincing, e.g., TSGM in line 156.
The captions of Fig 2,3 provide zero information. Many notations are introduced without definition, e.g., x_cont in line 192. Overall clarity can be further improved.
The significance is hard to parse due to limited clarity. It is lacking due to its assembly nature. Additionally, the correctness of the experimental evaluation is questioned.

The work lacks innovative methodology. Similar ideas for tabular data, which arguably encompass time-series data, have been explored in existing works [1]. Despite some crucial technical differences, the high-level framework is a latent diffusion model that projects structured data to a latent space and uses a diffusion model to model the distribution of latent codes.

The majority of the experiments are limited to unconditional generation of time-series data, and it is unclear how the proposed model can be readily adapted to tasks with more practical applications, such as forecasting and imputation.
Inability to generate interpretable results, limiting applicability in high-stakes fields where stakeholders need to understand model decisions.
Pure focus on continuous data raises concerns about effectiveness on heterogeneous datasets that include categorical features.
Dependence on latent space reduction, with performance drop when feature sizes increase, raising concerns about scalability and robustness in high-dimensional settings.
